chief_complaint: Cardiovascular risk management and hypertension follow-up in an elderly patient with prior NSTEMI, chronic kidney disease, and hyperlipidemia.
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 74-year-old woman with a history of an acute NSTEMI in December 2015, longstanding essential hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a diagnosis of diabetic kidney disease with CKD stage 1 identified in December 2017. Since the MI, she has been maintained on dual antiplatelet therapy, beta‑blocker, ACE‑inhibitor/CCB combination, thiazide diuretic, and statins. No outpatient visits have been recorded after December 2017, and recent laboratory values (eGFR, lipid panel, HbA1c, BMI) are missing. She reports ongoing stress, limited social contact, and part‑time employment, which may affect adherence and overall health.

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include two episodes of viral sinusitis (2016, 2017), prior full-time employment (resolved 2017), past intimate partner abuse and social isolation (resolved 2016), and a medication review due (resolved 2017).
